note: Failure and revocation fixtures for the two-host world (Sprint 3.3). Each case names a scenario the suite drives against world.json and the rule it must fail closed on. Expectations are hand-written: the message fragment is the rule, not a snapshot of an implementation detail.

cases.name: a replayed report is refused
cases.why: A captured report is not a second report. The channel accepts each sequence once.

cases.name: a reordered report is refused
cases.why: An older sequence arriving late is a replay from the channel's point of view.

cases.name: a report signed by the other host's key is refused
cases.why: A compromised key for one host must not speak for another. The key belongs to one host.

cases.name: a forged report is refused and does not consume its sequence
cases.why: Failing closed means the forgery costs the real host nothing.

cases.name: a report signed by a revoked key is refused
cases.why: Revocation is immediate; a key that still signs is still refused.
cases.expect_contains: the credential is not usable at this instant

cases.name: a revoked key is not freed for re-enrollment
cases.why: Revocation that re-issues is not revocation. Another host offering the revoked key is refused by name, and the original host is refused a second identity.

cases.name: a compromised host stops at the channel and never reaches operations
cases.why: The pipeline order is the fail-closed property: nothing downstream is asked about a report the channel refused.
cases.expect_contains: the credential is not usable at this instant

cases.name: a replayed desired state is refused
cases.why: A captured state is not a new instruction to become something.

cases.name: a desired state for the other host is refused
cases.why: The audience is the authorization; a redirected document is not configuration.

cases.name: a tampered desired state is refused
cases.why: The body is the configuration: changing it must break the signature.

cases.name: a forged desired state is refused
cases.why: A state nobody signed is a suggestion, not configuration.

cases.name: an expired desired state is refused
cases.why: Configuration has a lifetime; a host that has been away does not adopt a stale world forever.

cases.name: a revoked host's desired state is still verifiable but its reports are not
cases.why: Revocation cuts the host's voice, not the manager's: the host can still read what it was asked to become, and that is not a way back in.
